trust_decision.summary: The public tunnel server decides which request path is relayed to the client's local service. It forwards the percent-decoded r.URL.Path instead of the escaped path. The client then pastes that decoded path into a URL string, so encoded dot-segments, slashes and '?' reach the local origin as real path structure.

landing_point.why: The summary names openhole-server and a URL-decoded request path. The only server-side code that reads the request path for proxying is handlePublicProxy.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP: any request to <subdomain>.<PublicTunnelDomain> routed via internal/server/server.go:53-58 (handlePublicProxy)
Client tunnel read loop: websocket 'request' message -> internal/client/client.go:134,158 ForwardToLocal (an exported function in an internal package)
fix_sites.module_kind: client-side local forwarder (separate binary cmd/openhole, separate package internal/client)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: internal/client/local_proxy.go:20-23,37 (client binary rebuilds the URL with Sprintf from the relayed path; fix.diff:34-54)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names openhole-server, so a solver who switches the server to EscapedPath() can argue the client is a different component. They can also argue it only receives trusted messages from the server, and that its Sprintf just mirrors whatever the server sends.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate percent-encoded paths (for example /a%2fb, encoded spaces or unicode) must reach the local service byte-for-byte, and ordinary paths and the query string must pass through unchanged. If a fix rejects or strips '%' sequences, or path.Clean()s the path, it breaks apps that rely on encoded slashes. Re-escaping the path also double-encodes it. Both behaviours are asserted in fix.diff:101-131 and fix.diff:183-201.

O6_input_shapes: encoded slash %2f inside a segment (fix.diff:123, fix.diff:190)
query kept separate via RawQuery rather than string concatenation (fix.diff:52-54)

O7_producer.where: internal/protocol/messages.go:37 (RequestMessage.Path JSON field carries the path across the websocket; parsed unvalidated at internal/protocol/framing.go:44-47)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second server-side forwarding path (for example a path-prefix tunnel mode or a /health passthrough) that builds RequestMessage.Path from r.URL.Path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleRequest already branches on decoded r.URL.Path. A maintainer adding path-based tunnel routing would naturally reuse r.URL.Path and strip a prefix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second client forwarder (for example an HTTPS-local or retry/fallback path) that rebuilds the URL with fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s:%d%s", ...).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The client has one hard-coded http scheme. Adding a local TLS option is a plausible feature that would duplicate the Sprintf URL construction.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal via decode/re-encode differential in a reverse-proxy tunnel (parser differential on path identity)
